output.brief:
Owen, the fall in incidents is not real. Analysts still confirm about 36–37 incidents a month, the same as before the migration. But 47 of the 73 confirmed cases in Sep–Oct were switched to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" by the Brackwater integration account. Each switch came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just before the 4-hour deadline. Those cases then vanish from the incident count and the containment metrics. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp. That is why Brackwater shows 100% containment and a falling count. Alert volume is unchanged, and the monitoring queue has grown from 40 to 96.

What I can't tell yet is why. A known connector bug (advisory TXA-2026-14, affecting the version you run) fits the timing. Deliberate relabelling to earn the bonus also fits. Don't assume either.

Next steps:
- Don't approve the IR retainer cut or the 60k bonus.
- Reinstate the 47 cases as incidents, and have your team and Halvard check containment on each.
- Remove the integration role's category-edit rights, and upgrade the connector or drop the category field from it.
- Check the API gateway log (source host and user-agent) to see whether the connector or a person made the changes.
- Hold off on service credits until you know which it was.
